summary.objective: Decide whether to retain and investigate the current J12 connector or evaluate a replacement, without changing the board pinout.
summary.headline: Intermittent J12 disconnects during vibration are reported but not measured; no vibration test, retention-force measurement, candidate datasheet or independent review exists, so the evidence does not support approving any connector change yet.

sourceRegister.name: Field observation note — Rover Alpha J12 (synthetic)

anchors.excerpt: Operators reported intermittent J12 connector disconnects during vibration on the test track on three separate days.
Each report describes the drive controller losing its link to the sensor harness for one to three seconds and then recovering.
No measured test result is supplied with this note. No vibration profile, accelerometer data or connector retention measurement was recorded.
The reports do not identify whether the J12 shell, the contacts or the harness strain relief released.
Recommendation from the field lead: investigate the connector change before the next deployment.
Constraint R1: Any connector change must preserve the existing board pinout so the controller firmware and the sensor harness remain unchanged.
Constraint R2: The replacement, if any, must be compatible with the existing drive controller board footprint.
The exact baseline revision of the controller board is not supplied in this note.
The pin mapping table and the compatibility measurements for any candidate connector are not supplied in this note.
Checklist item 1: Vibration-test result for the current J12 connector — ABSENT. No vibration test has been run or recorded.
Checklist item 2: Connector retention-force measurement — not recorded.
Checklist item 3: Candidate replacement connector datasheet — not supplied.
Checklist item 4: Independent engineering review — an independent engineering reviewer has not approved the change.
Note: Items marked absent or not recorded block any release decision until evidence is obtained.

knownFacts.statement: Operators reported intermittent J12 connector disconnects during vibration on the test track on three separate days.
Each report describes the drive controller losing its link to the sensor harness for one to three seconds and then recovering.
Constraint R1: any connector change must preserve the existing board pinout so the controller firmware and the sensor harness remain unchanged.
Constraint R2: any replacement must be compatible with the existing drive controller board footprint.
The field lead recommends investigating the connector change before the next deployment. This is a recommendation, not an approval.
No independent engineering reviewer has approved the change, and items marked absent or not recorded block any release decision until evidence is obtained.

alternatives.title: Retain the current J12 connector and investigate the root cause
alternatives.description: Keep the existing J12 connector and characterize the failure: run a recorded vibration test, measure retention force and identify whether the shell, contacts or harness strain relief released. Inference: if the root cause turns out to be harness strain relief or mating, it may be fixable without changing the connector. Neither outcome is evidenced yet.
prerequisites: Recorded vibration test of the current J12 connector
Identification of the released element (shell, contacts or strain relief)

alternatives.title: Evaluate a replacement connector that preserves pinout and footprint
alternatives.description: Identify and evaluate a candidate replacement connector. Its compatibility with the existing pinout (R1) and drive controller board footprint (R2) is unknown until a datasheet, pin mapping table and compatibility measurements are supplied. No candidate has been named.
prerequisites: Pin mapping table for the current J12
Compatibility measurements against the existing footprint
Baseline revision of the controller board

affectedArtifacts.label: J12 connector on the drive controller board
affectedArtifacts.basis: This is the connector in the reported disconnects and the subject of R2's footprint constraint.

affectedArtifacts.label: Sensor harness
affectedArtifacts.basis: The link to the sensor harness drops during the disconnects, and R1 requires the harness to remain unchanged.

affectedArtifacts.label: Drive controller board footprint (layout)
affectedArtifacts.basis: R2 says any replacement must be compatible with the existing drive controller board footprint.

affectedArtifacts.label: Controller firmware
affectedArtifacts.basis: R1 preserves the pinout so the controller firmware remains unchanged. A pinout change would affect it.

affectedArtifacts.label: J12 pin mapping table and harness strain relief documentation
affectedArtifacts.basis: Inference: these documents are needed to verify pinout preservation and to check strain relief as a possible release point. They are not supplied.

evidenceGaps.gap: No vibration-test result for the current J12 connector. No vibration profile or accelerometer data was recorded.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Without a recorded test, the reported disconnects cannot be reproduced or quantified, and any fix cannot be verified.

evidenceGaps.gap: No connector retention-force measurement has been recorded.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Retention force is needed to judge whether the current connector is mechanically inadequate or whether something else is causing the failure.

evidenceGaps.gap: The reports do not identify whether the J12 shell, the contacts or the harness strain relief released.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: The failure location decides whether changing the connector would address the cause at all.

evidenceGaps.gap: No candidate replacement connector datasheet or compatibility measurements have been supplied.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Without them, pinout (R1) and footprint (R2) compatibility of any replacement cannot be assessed.

evidenceGaps.gap: The pin mapping table and the exact baseline revision of the controller board are not supplied.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Pinout preservation cannot be verified against an unknown baseline and an unknown mapping.

evidenceGaps.gap: No independent engineering reviewer has approved the change.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Release requires independent engineering review. The absent items block any release decision.

reviewQuestions.question: What vibration profile and pass/fail criteria should be used to test the current J12 connector on the Rover Alpha demonstration unit?

reviewQuestions.question: Which element released during the disconnects: the J12 shell, the contacts or the harness strain relief?
reviewQuestions.prerequisite: Instrumented vibration test and teardown inspection (G1, G3)

reviewQuestions.question: What is the baseline revision of the drive controller board, and where is the authoritative J12 pin mapping table?

Who is the independent engineering reviewer, and what evidence will they require before approving any connector change for release?

nextAction.action: Run and record a vibration test of the current J12 connector, including retention-force measurement and identification of the released element, before selecting either alternative.
nextAction.requiredInput: Defined vibration profile for the test track, the current J12 connector and harness on the drive controller board, and instrumentation to detect link loss

limitations: Packet ready means the paid preparation artifact was delivered. It is not engineering approval, a completed test or permission to release hardware. Independent engineering review and relevant physical evidence remain required.
All three sources are labeled synthetic fixtures invented for demonstration. Statements from them are recorded as kind "synthetic fixture" and do not describe real field data.
No measured test result, vibration profile, retention measurement, part number or candidate datasheet was supplied. This packet does not assert any of them.
Baseline is Unknown. The controller board revision was not supplied.
The field lead's recommendation is recorded as source content, not as an approval or decision.
